# Kyoto 5-Day Slow-Tempo Trip Plan

A balanced Kyoto itinerary for **2 adults** from **2026-11-03 to 2026-11-07**, designed around **temples, food markets, easy walking, and lighter crowds**. I’m assuming your **USD 2,400 budget excludes flights** and covers lodging, local transit, food, and admissions for both travelers.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

### Day 1: Nov 3 — Higashiyama Welcome Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, then do a gentle first stroll around **Gion** and **Yasaka Shrine**.
- Afternoon: Visit **Kodaiji** and nearby lanes; keep the route short and use taxis if needed for any uphill stretch.
- Food: Early dinner in **Pontocho** or a simple set-meal place near Kawaramachi.
- Transit tip: Use a **taxi from station to hotel** if luggage is heavy; otherwise take Kyoto City Bus only for short hops.
- Estimated cost for 2: **USD 260–340**
  - Lodging: 180–240
  - Food: 50–70
  - Transit/admissions: 30–30

### Day 2: Nov 4 — Central Kyoto Temples and Markets
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: Start at **Nishiki Market** before it gets busy; snack gradually instead of doing one large meal.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning: Start at **Nishiki Market** before it gets busy; snack gradually instead of doing one large meal, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Walk to **Nijo Castle** and nearby flat streets; this keeps the day accessible and low-effort.
- Food: Market bites at Nishiki, then a relaxed lunch around **Shijo**.
- Transit tip: This is a good **walking + subway** day; use the subway for the longest segment and avoid bus congestion.
- Estimated cost for 2: **USD 250–330**
  - Lodging: 180–240
  - Food: 45–60
  - Transit/admissions: 25–30

### Day 3: Nov 5 — Arashiyama, Kept Gentle
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Go early to **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** and **Tenryu-ji** before peak crowds.
- Afternoon: Choose one easy add-on only: **Togetsukyo Bridge** and riverside seating, or a short boat/tea stop.
- Food: Lunch near Arashiyama station; keep the afternoon light.
- Transit tip: Take the **JR Sagano Line** or a taxi to reduce walking transfers; skip steep hillside spots.
- Estimated cost for 2: **USD 280–360**
  - Lodging: 180–240
  - Food: 50–70
  - Transit/admissions: 35–50

### Day 4: Nov 6 — Fushimi and Southern Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- Morning: Visit **Fushimi Inari** only for the lower shrine area and torii entrance; do not attempt the full mountain climb.
- Afternoon: Head to **Fushimi Sake District** for a calm canal-side walk and a tasting lunch.
- Food: Sake-friendly lunch or a tofu set meal in southern Kyoto.
- Transit tip: Use **JR** for Fushimi Inari and a **taxi** or local train for the sake district if walking energy is low.
- Estimated cost for 2: **USD 240–320**
  - Lodging: 180–240
  - Food: 45–60
  - Transit/admissions: 15–20

### Day 5: Nov 7 — Easy Exit Day
- Morning: Keep it simple with **To-ji Temple** or a final short market stop near Kyoto Station.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4f/Dry-sand_Zen_garden_made_of_beige_stripes_a_sunny_day_at_Higashiyama_Jisho-ji_Buddhist_temple_Ginkaku-ji_Kyoto_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning: Keep it simple with **To-ji Temple** or a final short market stop near Kyoto Station, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Check out, shop for snacks and souvenirs, then depart.
- Food: Brunch near the station so you can leave without rushing.
- Transit tip: Stay close to **Kyoto Station** on departure day to minimize transfers and luggage stress.
- Estimated cost for 2: **USD 160–240**
  - Lodging: 0–80 if you need a late checkout or luggage hold elsewhere
  - Food: 40–60
  - Transit/admissions: 20–30

## Budget Fit and Pace Check

| Item | Estimated Total for 2 | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Lodging | USD 720–1,040 | Mid-range hotel or ryokan-style stay, 4 nights |
| Food | USD 230–320 | Mix of market snacks, casual lunches, and simple dinners |
| Transit | USD 90–140 | Subway, JR, taxis for low-stress segments |
| Admissions | USD 60–110 | Temples, castle, and optional tastings |
| Buffer | USD 150–250 | Coffee, extra taxi, snacks, rain backup |
| Trip Total | **USD 1,250–1,860** | Leaves room under your USD 2,400 cap |

## Slower-Paced Alternative: Replace Day 3

If one traveler feels tired or you want to avoid Arashiyama crowds, swap Day 3 for this gentler version:

### Day 3 Alternative: Kyoto Station Area + Temples Without Hills
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Morning: Visit **To-ji Temple** and browse the surrounding flat streets.
- Afternoon: Spend time at **Kyoto Station** area, **Isetan**, or a café break instead of long sightseeing.
- Food: Casual lunch and an early dinner near your hotel.
- Transit tip: This is the easiest low-walking day; use **subway, taxi, or short bus rides** only.
- Estimated cost for 2: **USD 180–260**
